questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to Spain as i had Spanish for 3 years in high school and wanted to experience how it would be to live there. And i also wanted to go a country in the south europe with better weather than Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an really good experience and loved the city and the rest of Northern Spain.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat easy. Some of their website was useful, but finding information about courses was difficult because some of it was only offered in Spanish even though the course was offered in English

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international office at Sarriko is very helpful. It was easy to get help through mail and also by showing up physically.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was an introduction day where you were showed around which made it easier to find the rooms the first couple of days.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think it was alright. However do it sooner rather than later even though the host university says  you can wait till arrival. All the good and cheap places will be rented out to other people. I found housing through Happy Erasmus, which was okay, but i think you can find cheaper accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It will be smart to live close to a metro station as Sarriko is a good walk away from city center. Otherwise it is possible to rent bikes, which makes the transportation easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult as some of the course description was only in Spanish even though the course was offered in English and other course description was impossible to find. So a bit confusing, but the international office was very helpful. Also there wasn't a lot of courses offered in English.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you could register from home in June, and then also when you got down there, but a lot of the good courses was already full.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the international office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat successful. I got 3 out of 5 courses i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be quick to apply for courses in June, because the good ones might be filled in September.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: For some courses the level was really easy and for some it was quite hard. Also because of the language barrier and they just do things differently than what we are used to in Denmark.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3 of the courses i had was really easy and more like high school courses, also in the way it was thought. 2 of the courses were a bit more difficult, but also because the teachers were quite bad.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: more class room teaching than what we are used to. They want people to participate and some courses have mandatory class attendance.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Economics, Regional Economics, Economic History of Contemporary Spain, Financial Management: Investments, Statistics and business analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Economics, Regional Economics, Economic History of Contemporary Spain. These courses were quite easy and also a bit interesting. For example have not seen a course called regional economics at UCPH.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Did not encounter any unexpected cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out to eat was really inexpensive, while groceries were more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There weren't any

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are two different Erasmus groups that host events and such for exchange students. I would really recommend participating in those as it is a good way to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Northern Spain. It is really easy to go by busses, but also to rent cars. If possible go to Picos de Europa, it is amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy and difficult. It was a bit hard that everything in Spain starts around 9 pm, when you have school at 8 in the morning. But i really liked that everything was open until late. It made the day longer.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is a bit difficult as most of them only speak Spanish

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They eat a lot later than what we are used to

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked that you go out all the time. It is easy and cheap to drink coffee and wine in bars

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Check how the exams are, apply for courses quickly and also search for housing earlier than august.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There more school than what we are used to, which i wasn't prepared for.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people i met and living in Bilbao.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To create a daily routine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
